corpus.note: the harness serves an asset copy of the corpus taken from the worktree. A Windows checkout writes CRLF, so the file was normalised back to the committed LF blob before the final harness build: the served bytes and the committed blob hash to the same value, which is also the hash the Liber-side observation records (fixturesSha256).

harness.apkSha256IsNotPortableBetweenBuilds: apksigner output is not byte-stable between builds of these same sources; the sources' hashes and the toolchain versions are the stable identity, the APK hash is an artifact of this build
harness.suspendEntryPoints: driven with kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking through a java.lang.reflect.Proxy over kotlin.jvm.functions.Function2, whose continuation is handed to the frozen suspend method. getChapterListAwait's JVM name is mangled (getChapterListAwait-BWLJW6A) because its kotlin.Result return type is an inline value class, and the payload is read through the synthetic unbox-impl method; getOrNull is an inlined extension and is not callable.
harness.deferredToTheMainLooper: Instrumentation.onCreate posts the run to the main looper: the frozen HTTP stack and its cookie store are built by the target application, which is created after onCreate. The run itself is on its own thread because runBlocking blocks the caller.
harness.needSaveFalse: getContentAwait is called with needSave=false. A synthetic corpus has no row in the frozen application's database, so persisting the chapter is a storage side effect outside the compared surface; every other argument is the default the product's own call site uses.

run.freezeNote: MIUI's power manager freezes the frozen application's uid about three seconds after the process starts; the run finishes in well under that, and the report is written before the replay server is torn down so a freeze cannot lose the evidence.

divergences.reason: R8 is the frozen reader rendering prefix; the product compares the post-rule text before paragraph indentation.

notCompared: requests[].headers.accept-encoding — platform-generated: the contract ignores Host, Content-Length, Accept-Encoding and Connection unless the source sets them (book-source-differential-contract.md, Matching Rules -> Requests), and the SLICE-01 source sets only X-Slice-Corpus. Every other header name on every request is compared by R3.

requests[].headers.connection — platform-generated: the contract ignores Host, Content-Length, Accept-Encoding and Connection unless the source sets them (book-source-differential-contract.md, Matching Rules -> Requests), and the SLICE-01 source sets only X-Slice-Corpus. Every other header name on every request is compared by R3.

requests[].headers.host — platform-generated: the contract ignores Host, Content-Length, Accept-Encoding and Connection unless the source sets them (book-source-differential-contract.md, Matching Rules -> Requests), and the SLICE-01 source sets only X-Slice-Corpus. Every other header name on every request is compared by R3.

stages.bookInfo.tocUrl — the golden carries the resolved TOC URL the frozen entity holds; the product's book-information evidence shape does not record it. The chapters it leads to are compared by R7, and the TOC request is in R2.

stages.toc.chapters[].url (as stored) — the frozen entity stores the raw rule output (a relative path) and resolves it when used; the product stores the resolved URL. The resolved values are what R7 compares (chaptersAbsolute against the Liber url), and the request trace shows both sides resolving to the same URLs.

requests[].body — every request in this corpus is a GET with an empty body, so both evidence files record an empty string and there are no body bytes to compare. The contract compares request body bytes strictly, so a corpus that declares a POST has to extend this row before it can pass.

state.*, cleanup.*, serverErrors — frozen-side observations with no counterpart in the Liber evidence: state repeats what R4/R7/R8 compare; cleanup is this harness's own replay-server teardown (openConnections, serverClosed), not a source-observable cleanup effect; serverErrors is the replay server's own error list.

liber.scenario, liber.oracle, liber.fixturesPath/fixturesSha256, liber.libraryPath/librarySha256 — Liber-side fields the comparator does not read: `scenario` is the product run's own shape check (the request sequence it describes is recomputed for R9 from `requests` and the corpus `expectedRequests`), `oracle` records that the observation was recorded before a golden existed, and the `fixtures*`/`library*` fields identify the input bytes. The corpus bytes are hashed and checked against the manifest pin instead.
platform, fingerprint, recordedAt — provenance of the two runs, recorded in each evidence file and its manifest; not a compatibility observation.

gaps: The Android destination row of R13 stays not-run: the product has no Android application (P4). This golden is the frozen half of R13 only.
R12 is promoted by CI run 35125476388 for the desktop destination rows; this evidence tree does not replace that CI record.

The corpus' own gaps, listed in fixtures.json and docs/compatibility/first-slice.md, are unchanged: one source, no redirect/non-2xx/POST/WebView/JSON/XPath/rule-JS row, no concurrency or rate limit, no chapter variables or login state, no failure path, no second book.
needSave=false leaves the frozen reader's chapter-persistence side effect unobserved.
